title: Topic 02, Part 01 - Database Entities

best.what: what an entity/table is and how to pick which attributes belong on it

why: clean, jargon-light explanation of what a table should represent (single theme, chosen attributes only), maps directly onto one-tab-per-thing Sheet design.

title: Topic 02, Part 07 - Foreign Keys and Relationships Between Tables

best.what: foreign keys link two tables via matching ID columns, and referential integrity stops you pointing at a row that doesn't exist

why: first 15 min nails exactly how kids will link Sheet tabs by ID columns; the remaining 12+ min is a live SQL Server Management Studio point-and-click demo (plus an off-topic date-format aside) that doesn't transfer to Apps Script/Sheets.

title: Topic 04, Part 06 - Conceptual Crow's Foot Relationship Symbols

best.what: one-vs-many relationship notation, i.e. deciding which side of a link the ID column should live on

why: short, concrete way to decide whether a link between two Sheet tabs is one-to-one or one-to-many before wiring up ID columns; the line-ending symbols are the whole lesson so it needs the drawing.

title: Topic 06, Part 06 - Introduction to Resource Locking

best.what: why simultaneous edits need exclusive locks, via a store-exclusive-access analogy and an inventory example, plus what deadlock is

why: this is the exact concept behind LockService (exclusive access to avoid lost updates, and the deadlock risk that comes with it), explained entirely with everyday analogies, no SQL Server demo in this one.

title: Elements of the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

best.what: breaking a software project into phases, then work packages, then tasks

why: clear phase -> work-package -> task breakdown using a software example; beats CWgT38w7aSU's 21-minute construction-bridge WBS lecture on the same idea, but PMP terms like 'work package' still need translating for teens.

title: Functional and Non-functional Requirements | What is the difference between the two?

best.what: functional requirements (what it does) vs non-functional (implicit quality expectations: speed, reliability, ease of use)

why: a genuinely useful, jargon-light distinction for scoping a solo app -- what to build vs. the quality bar it's expected to meet -- explained with website/car examples a teen gets immediately.

title: Scope Creep
why: same core idea as VVS90RgEunw (small uncontrolled changes snowball) but wrapped in heavier corporate 'change management process' framing and no actionable prevention tips; beaten by VVS90RgEunw's version.

title: Scope Creep | Causes of Scope Creep | How to prevent Scope Creep

best.what: prevent scope creep by sticking to your original goal (bridge-vs-boat example) and writing down what's explicitly excluded

why: "stick to your goal, write down what you're NOT building" is exactly what a solo 4-8 week teen project needs, but it's delivered in PMP-exam language (change management, stakeholder sign-off) a guide would need to strip out; beats _ufV2iBlOeI's take on the same topic.

title: Gold Plating in Project Management (PMP)

best.what: adding an unrequested feature because you assume it'll make the product better -- and why that's a bad idea even with good intentions

why: names exactly the "I added this cool thing nobody asked for" trap solo hobbyist coders fall into constantly; short, concrete, no PMP jargon needed to get it.

title: Define Scope Process
why: first minute is a channel self-promo tour, and the actual content just restates 'write down what's in and out of scope' more abstractly and less usefully than VVS90RgEunw's bridge/boat example.

title: #2 Objectives of a Project: Scientific Management of Goals | Project Planning & Control
why: construction/real-estate cost-profit framing (Chennai metro, ISO 21500, IS 15883, safety codes) with little that transfers to a teen's solo app project beyond a briefly-mentioned plan-do-check-act cycle.

title: #8 Basics of Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) | Project Planning & Control
why: same WBS concept as QLoYKsOP9Ig but stretched into a 21-minute Socratic classroom dialogue built around a labeled bridge diagram (precast piles, abutments, pile caps) that needs civil-engineering knowledge kids don't have; beaten by QLoYKsOP9Ig's shorter software-project version.

title: #9 Tools for Time Management | Project Planning & Control

best.what: use the simplest planning tool the job needs -- a list or calendar is often enough; don't reach for Gantt/PERT/Monte Carlo just because they're sophisticated

why: "match your planning tool to the job, and get more granular as the deadline nears" is a genuinely useful right-sizing idea for a solo project, but it's loose classroom Q&A that a guide would need to tighten into a plain tip.

title: User Research Full Course 2026 [FREE] | User Research UX Design Tutorial For Beginners | Simplilearn
why: the sampled first 30 min is mostly a paid Figma/AI-design-certification ad plus rambling classroom banter (Blinkit, Apple Watch anecdotes) around a thin, unstructured pass at qualitative/quantitative/behavioral research types; adds nothing the library's existing CareerFoundry user-research video doesn't already cover more tightly.

title: Usability Evaluation and Testing in UI UX | Usability Testing Tutorial for Beginners | Simplilearn

best.what: Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics, each paired with one instantly-recognizable app example (Google Drive, Airbnb, Word, Facebook, Amazon, Photoshop, Gmail, Spotify, GitHub)

why: the heuristics-with-familiar-app-examples segment is concrete and teen-legible in a way a plain checklist page isn't, but it's buried in long personal tangents and a live Airbnb walkthrough that cuts off mid-exercise; needs heavy trimming to be worth using.

title: Visual Design And Wire Framing Full Course 2026 | Visual Design Wire Framing Tutorial | Simplilearn

best.what: Gestalt principles (proximity, similarity, continuity, closure, figure-ground, symmetry) each with an iconic example -- the FedEx logo's hidden arrow, Google's symmetrical homepage, Pinterest's column layout

why: solid, concrete visual/Gestalt design principles with iconic examples that would genuinely help teens critique their own UI, but the sampled 30 minutes never reaches wireframing (the title's other half) and is diluted by long personal tangents (Cracker Barrel logo, New Coke); needs trimming.
